findings.summary: Andrew Dickson White (1832–1918) was an American historian and educator who co-founded Cornell University and served as its first president for nearly two decades. He expanded college curricula and served as U.S. ambassador to Germany and Russia. He was a key proponent of the conflict thesis, arguing science and religion have historically been in conflict, detailed in his 800-page work History of the Warfare of Science with Theology in Christendom. He also served in the New York State Senate and held diplomatic posts. His efforts sought to broaden the scope of higher education.

mechanisms.title: Curriculum expansion at Cornell
mechanisms.explanation: White expanded the scope of college curricula at Cornell University, introducing new fields and approaches beyond traditional classical education.

mechanisms.explanation: White was a key proponent of the conflict thesis, arguing that science and religion have historically been in conflict, which he attempted to prove in his 800-page work History of the Warfare of Science with Theology in Christendom.
